major_concerns: Vendor-specific device images and CLI semantics may be proprietary or unavailable, reducing reproducibility and external validity.
Deterministic verifiers (e.g., Batfish) may miss semantic runtime failures leading to optimistic safety estimates.
Automated repair loops can introduce subtle semantic errors that verifiers do not detect; emulator fidelity may not reflect production behavior.
required_design_repairs: Restrict vendor set to open-source or freely redistributable network OSes (e.g., FRR, Open vSwitch, containerized network stacks) or explicitly document licensing and provide synthetic vendor-variant generators if proprietary images cannot be redistributed.

Specify and justify the mapping from vendor-CLI to verifier input (use canonical intermediate representation such as YANG/Netconf/structured templates) and include parser/test-suite artifacts to allow verification of parsing correctness.

Pre-register verifier coverage tests and a verifier-failure audit procedure (manual adjudication policy only for infrastructure failures), and add additional semantic checks (e.g., reachability test harness) to complement verifier outputs.

major_concerns: LLM uncertainty signals (token log-probs) may not be available or well calibrated from hosted APIs, undermining threshold policies.
Cost proxy and verifier-latency models may not reflect realistic deployment economics and load-dependent latencies.
Policy evaluation depends on realistic latency distributions and verifier throughput under concurrency; simulation must be justified.
required_design_repairs: Specify concretely how uncertainty will be estimated given available model APIs (e.g., sampling-based entropy, multiple-sample agreement, or use of model-provided token-prob when available) and preregister calibration procedures (reliability diagrams, temperature scaling).
Define the monetary-cost proxy and sensitivity analyses mapping proxy to real cost; preregister alternative proxies and report sensitivity results.
Pre-register verifier latency distributions and stress-test scenarios (e.g., load-sweep) or justify synthetic latency models with reference telemetry or prior measurements.

major_concerns: High dual-use/ethical risk from producing adversarial/backdoor patterns that enable unsafe behavior if published verbatim.
Creating realistic backdoors may require model fine-tuning or privileged access (not permitted) or many API calls; feasibility must be constrained and documented.
Reproducibility suffers if adversarial patterns depend on nondeterministic model behavior or proprietary model internals.
required_design_repairs: Add an explicit ethical-risk mitigation plan and safe-release policy: redact or abstract concrete trigger payloads in public artifacts, include disclosure controls, and only publish high-level taxonomy and sanitized examples.

Constrain experiments to non-fine-tuning attack classes (prompt-level injection/backdoor patterns) and/or use locally simulated/synthetic models when possible; preregister exact adversary classes, query budgets, and abstention for dangerous outputs.
Define and preregister rules for responsible artifact release (redaction, withheld prompts) and include an IRB/ethics-style checklist in the execution manifest.

major_concerns: Composite-score training risks overfitting to synthetic task bank and may not generalize to production distributions.
Canary simulation fidelity and the definition of rollback-success probability need concrete specification to avoid ambiguous labels.
Weight-learning and threshold selection can introduce optimistic bias unless cross-validation and held-out test are strictly preregistered.
required_design_repairs: Pre-register the exact submetric definitions, training/validation/test splits, regularization strategy (e.g., penalized logistic regression), and cross-validation procedure.
Specify canary topology size and fidelity constraints; include ablation plan and out-of-sample generalization checks with bootstrapped CIs.
Preregister decision-threshold selection rules and include decision-curve analysis and calibration reporting (Brier score, reliability diagrams).

major_concerns: Constructed deceptive descriptions may lack ecological validity relative to real-world marketplace tactics.
Runtime capability probes risk inducing side effects if they execute unsafe operations; probe design must be non-invasive and safe.
Evaluation depends on realistic tool catalogs and agent architectures; results may not generalize to heterogeneous real registries.
required_design_repairs: Source real open registry descriptions as the baseline (scraped with permission) and generate deceptive variants via controlled paraphrase/overclaim transformations rather than inventing attack templates.
Design runtime probes to be non-invasive (read-only capability checks, schema/response validation) and preregister probe safety rules; ensure probes never execute privileged/write operations.
Pre-register agent selection mechanism and provide reproducible agent prompt templates, and include sensitivity analyses over registry size and deception types.
